methods.label: Find the height, then make a quarter-turn
methods.explanation:
Since \(BO\) lies on the \(x\)-axis, the right angle at \(B\) makes \(AB\) vertical. Write \(h=AB>0\); the first-quadrant condition then gives \(A=(5,h)\).

In right triangle \(OAB\), the leg \(AB\) is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle, so it is half the hypotenuse: \(OA=2h\). The Pythagorean theorem now gives
\[
5^2+h^2=(2h)^2,
\]
so \(3h^2=25\). Taking the positive root because \(h\) is a length,
\[
h=\frac{5\sqrt3}{3}.
\]
A \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation turns a rightward displacement into an upward displacement and an upward displacement into a leftward displacement. Thus it sends \((x,y)\) to \((-y,x)\). The image of \(A\) is therefore
\[
\boxed{\left(-\frac{5\sqrt3}{3},\,5\right)},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
